# Code Map — Backend

One shared .NET API: one class library per domain, composed in the Api gateway. Every
domain library has the same shape — Domain/ (aggregates), Application/ (vertical use-case
slices), Infrastructure/ (DI root, Endpoints/, Persistence/).

**Migrations: DO NOT READ files under Infrastructure/Persistence/Migrations/ — generated 1,600–2,000-line Designer files. The map records count + latest name only.**

- Kernel/Roles.cs is the only source of role strings (case-sensitive, ordinal matching) — never string literals.
- Messaging/Sender.cs is the hand-rolled mediator (no MediatR). EventBus: delivery is outbox polling (OutboxPollingConsumer); RabbitMQ carries only BusPublicationRegistry entries — first live entry (constructed in SharedServiceCollectionExtensions.cs): booking.booking-day-confirmed → Trips.
- RabbitMqIntegrationEventConsumer pushes AmbientTenant from the event's TenantId payload BEFORE resolving the handler scope — ModuleDbContext captures the tenant at construction, so a scope built earlier would silently filter out every row.
<!-- notes:shared:end -->

<!-- notes:trips:start -->
- Domain/Trips/Trip.cs owns the billing-driven lifecycle: ReadyForBilling → Invoiced → Completed (Completed means paid); CloseWithoutBilling is the write-off path.
- Shipments are the cargo aggregate: billing client is set on the shipment itself, never inherited from a trip; ShipmentLegs reference trips by id only (no navigation into trips.trips).
- Route timetables live on RouteStop as two nullable OFFSETS (Outbound/ReturnOffsetMinutes, minutes after that leg's departure) inside the existing `stops` jsonb — no columns, so adding them needed only an empty migration. Offsets stay attached to their stop for the whole snapshot's life, including onto trips; the leg's TripDirection selects which one applies, so every stop-list reversal (TripGenerationWorker's returnStops, Trip.CreateDeadheadReturn) copies BOTH through unchanged rather than swapping them. Route.Validate enforces per leg: all-or-nothing, first stop 0, strictly increasing — outbound ascending Order, return descending.
- Schedule exceptions (special dates: skip / extra run / time override) are child rows of ScheduleTemplate, one per date, applied at generation time only — never to trips already materialized; past dates are allowed on purpose. Cargo-service templates normalize SeatsCapacity/SeatsMinimum to null (TripServiceTypeExtensions.IsCargoService decides).
- Integration/BookingDayConfirmedIntegrationEventHandler is the one handler here that arrives via RabbitMQ (chain-reaction), not outbox polling: Trip.ScheduleFromBooking creates the community trip (carries BookingDayId) and TripScheduledFromBooking flows back to Booking via the outbox.
<!-- notes:trips:end -->

<!-- notes:fleet:start -->
- Projections/FleetProjectionRegistry.cs is the single registry of every Fleet projection + same-module OnEvent reaction — DI (AddFleet) and the integration-test fixture both compose from it.
- MaintenancePlanDocumentMapping.cs holds the items/overhauls jsonb mapping shared by the maintenance_plans aggregate table and its rm_ read-model mirror, so write/read shapes can't drift.
- A defect has no id — it lives in the inspection's `defects` jsonb, so it is addressed by (InspectionId, Item) everywhere (Enter/Amend reject duplicate Items to keep that key unique); migration 20260912225642_AddDefectResolution is deliberately EMPTY because the resolution fields only change that jsonb payload.
- Resolution is final, never reopened: a returning fault is a NEW defect pointing back via RecurrenceOfInspectionId, Amend MERGES resolution stamps instead of replacing them, and completing a work order resolves every still-open defect on the inspection that generated it (Recurrence itself is derived per read by VehicleDefectReadService, never stored).
<!-- notes:fleet:end -->

- Allocations/CopyFromPeriod checks `AllowsPlanChanges` on the TARGET only — a Closed period is a legal source by design, since copying last period's plan into a fresh Draft is the whole feature; do not add the symmetric guard. Per line it skips already-planned codes (never overwriting a justification somebody wrote) and retired/deleted ones, and `CopyInto` carries the amount but not the justification, so a copied line still has to be argued.
<!-- notes:budgeting:end -->

<!-- notes:billing:start -->
A QuickBooks prep worksheet, not an invoice system of record: the module prices completed
uninvoiced round trips at the contract rate and the numbers are keyed into QBO by hand (no QBO
API call anywhere). It computes **no tax** — `Invoice.TotalCad` is the plain sum of its lines,
with no subtotal/GST split and no rate field; QuickBooks owns all tax calculation. Lifecycle is
Draft → EnteredInQbo → Void, with no Sent/Paid/AR-aging.
<!-- notes:billing:end -->

- /api/notifications requires the DispatchAccess policy (Owner/Dispatcher/Supervisor); send validates the template's service type + client pin against the trip (ServiceTypeMismatch/ClientMismatch in EmailTemplateErrors).
- {{PickupTime}}/{{DropoffTime}} resolve per recipient: PickupEmailRenderer prefers RecipientInput.PickupTime/DropoffTime and falls back to the command's trip-level ones (blank counts as absent). The times themselves are computed frontend-side from the route timetable — Dispatcher/lib/timetable.ts — because Notifications never queries Trips; trip context stays an opaque snapshot composed by the dispatcher's screen.
- Integration/BookingDayRevertedIntegrationEventHandler is the module's first event-driven send (outbox-polled): "community trip at risk" emails to the event's recipient snapshot, built-in body unless an active CommunityBookingAtRisk template overrides; dispatch ids derive from EventId+chunk index so redelivery sends nothing twice.
<!-- notes:notifications:end -->

- Persistence deliberately skips the rm_ read-model/projection pattern: read services query the aggregate tables directly, and all repository/read-service interfaces + impls are consolidated into single Repositories.cs / ReadServices.cs files (both in Abstractions/ and Persistence/).
- BookingDay lifecycle (Unconfirmed/Confirmed/Reverted): BookingDayThresholdService recomputes sold-vs-minimum INSIDE the confirm/cancel booking transaction and never saves itself; confirming publishes booking.booking-day-confirmed (the RabbitMQ chain-reaction event), reverting is gated by CancellationWindow + the Guarantee (Gift-a-Seat) flag.
<!-- notes:booking:end -->
